title: Lesson 1 - OmniStudio Solution Overview: The OmniStudio Toolset and Ecosystem
description: Describe the Omnistudio solution and common customer use case scenarios in different industries (telco, energy, healthcare, public sector, etc.)

questions.question: A consulting team is evaluating OmniStudio for a client that needs a guided multi-step application flow with a reusable data-integration layer. Which statement best describes how the OmniStudio tools relate to each other?
options: Each tool is a standalone product with its own runtime and metadata model.
The tools share one runtime and metadata model and are designed to compose, so a FlexCard can call an OmniScript and an OmniScript can invoke an Integration Procedure.
The tools are only usable independently and cannot reference each other's artifacts.
The tools replace the Salesforce platform's native security and sharing model.
questions.explanation: The defining architectural point of OmniStudio is that FlexCards, OmniScripts, Integration Procedures, and Data Mappers share a single runtime and metadata model and are built to compose. Option A is wrong because they are not standalone products with separate runtimes. Option C is wrong because cross-referencing artifacts is a core feature. Option D is wrong because OmniStudio runs on top of the platform's security model rather than replacing it.

questions.question: A client asks whether OmniStudio can be used to build a guided quote-and-application journey for a high-volume sales team. Which consideration is most important for the architect to communicate about the declarative-first design?
options: OmniStudio requires custom Apex for every step of the journey.
OmniStudio is best suited to high-volume, form-heavy, multi-step processes, and the declarative tools cover the common path while unusual logic still needs Apex.
OmniStudio only works for single-page forms and cannot handle multi-step flows.
OmniStudio bypasses object permissions so any user can see any record.
questions.explanation: OmniStudio's value is strongest for high-volume, form-heavy, multi-step processes where guided steps and reusable components reduce custom page maintenance. Option A is wrong because the common path is declarative, not Apex-heavy. Option C is wrong because multi-step flows are a primary use case. Option D is wrong because OmniStudio respects, not bypasses, the platform security model.

questions.question: A partner plans to build an OmniStudio solution once and install it into many customer orgs. Why does the metadata-based design of OmniStudio support this model?
options: Because OmniStudio artifacts are compiled into a single binary that cannot be reused.
Because every OmniStudio artifact is metadata that can be versioned, deployed through change sets or a DevOps pipeline, and reused across orgs.
Because each customer org must rebuild every artifact from scratch.
Because OmniStudio artifacts are stored only in the customer's browser cache.
questions.explanation: OmniStudio artifacts are metadata, so they can be versioned, deployed through change sets or a DevOps pipeline, and reused across orgs, which is exactly what a build-once-install-many partner model needs. Option A is wrong because there is no single compiled binary. Option C is wrong because reuse across orgs is the point. Option D is wrong because artifacts live in the org's metadata, not the browser cache.
